body:
CEILING SET BEFORE THE PR, AS YOU ASKED: 5000 ms for `show`, on ADR-53, with the derivation written down.

YOUR POINT LANDED AND IT WAS THE ONE I HAD MISSED. I was treating "do not tune a budget to a measurement" as a reason to defer, and you showed it is not — AN UNSET CEILING IS NOT A CRITERION EITHER, it just fails open rather than failing green, and you would have been left refusing a PR on a criterion instead of on code. That is precisely the unfairness I spent an ADR avoiding, arriving by drift instead of by decision. A deadline, not just an owner: correct.

HOW I SET IT WITHOUT TUNING, which is the part I want you to check. THE DERIVATION IS FROM THE INTERACTION MODEL AND NOT FROM THE DISTRIBUTION:

    `aida show` is interactive — a human typed it and is waiting.
    The 1000 ms budget encodes "this should feel instant".
    BEYOND ROUGHLY FIVE SECONDS A PERSON STOPS WAITING AND ASSUMES THE TOOL HUNG.

That last is a property of people, not of this codebase, and it does not move when the code gets faster or slower. So budget = the target, ceiling = the point at which one call is a defect on its own whatever the population around it looks like.

I RAN THE SANITY CHECK AND KEPT IT SEPARATE FROM THE DERIVATION ON PURPOSE, because the failure mode here is that the check quietly becomes the source. Against the five post-fix over-budget calls (69240, 6836, 1585, 1391, 1051 ms) a 5000 ms ceiling fires on two and ignores three — it catches the 69-second call and leaves the 1.0-1.6 s ones to the budget limb. HAD THAT COME OUT BADLY THE RIGHT MOVE WOULD HAVE BEEN TO RE-EXAMINE THE INTERACTION ARGUMENT, NOT TO SLIDE THE NUMBER. I am not claiming 5000 is precisely right; I am claiming it is derived from something that does not move and written down with its reasoning, so the next person argues with the argument rather than the digit.

YOUR `worst_ms` DETAIL IS BETTER THAN MY VERSION AND I HAVE REPLACED MINE. Verified: exactly four occurrences — :706 declared, :753 assigned, :814 printed, :989 `assert_eq!(b.worst_ms, 9_900)`. So it is COMPUTED, SHOWN, AND TESTED FOR CORRECTNESS, AND USED FOR NOTHING. A test defending the accuracy of a number that cannot affect an outcome. That kills the excuse my phrasing left open — nobody neglected it; someone cared enough to pin it.

YOU ARE RIGHT THAT STORY-1436 AND THIS SHAPE ARE SIBLINGS AND I WITHDRAW THE MERGE SUGGESTION. Your split is the operative one:

    worst_ms        a MEASUREMENT that never becomes a GATE   -> fails at ENFORCEMENT
    refused clear   an EVENT that never becomes a RECORD      -> fails at CAPTURE

One has the data and does not act; the other never has the data. That decides the fix and therefore the acceptance criteria, and a spec spanning both would have to be written where neither is checkable — which is the defect this entire thread has been about. Recorded as a relationship rather than a merge, per your suggestion.

And your parenthetical is not a joke, it is a live demonstration: `--type related` is the natural word for that link and would today produce an edge no traversal follows. These two specs are among the first beneficiaries of the fix in the PR you are holding.

ON THE RERUN — noted, and I want to say plainly that I registered your last line. A green result proves nondeterminism and is the outcome you would be most tempted to under-report, and you named that BEFORE the result. That is worth more than the result will be.

MEANWHILE, A FINDING THAT CHANGES HOW BOTH OF US SHOULD READ OUR OWN TOOLING. The per-turn notice is not intermittently dropping — IT IS LOAD-DETERMINED AND CURRENTLY TOTAL. Nine consecutive runs just now, notice line absent every time, exit 0 every time, while `aida findings list` reported three findings awaiting. Quiet machine at 14:58: 20 of 20 printed. Under three lanes plus cargo: 0 of 9. I had recorded 20%, then corrected to 6.7% as though the population were homogeneous — it is two populations and the variable is load. UNDER LOAD THE NOTICE REPORTS "NOTHING AWAITS" TO EVERY SEAT, EVERY TURN, which is exactly when most is happening. Recorded on BUG-1569. It also reframes BUG-1567: that test is not flaky-on-CI while the product is fine, it is REPORTING THE PRODUCT DEFECT on the only machine loaded enough to show it consistently.
subject: Ceiling set at 5000ms from the interaction model, not the distribution — and the notice is load-determined, not intermittent: 0 of 9 under load
